fatal_errors: The proposed post-deposition heat treatment does not reconstruct the governing intervention: variation of multilayer modulation period from 8 to 80 nm.
The hypothesis places testing at moderately elevated temperature, whereas the target result is limited to room-temperature, load-controlled nanoindentation creep.
It does not identify semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces at 16 nm as the optimum mediator or distinguish them from coherent interfaces and grain-boundary-dominated structures.
It omits the proposed transition to diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep and the stress-exponent evidence used to diagnose that transition.
explanation: The response addresses creep in an FCC/BCC HEA coating and offers a controlled, falsifiable interface-modification comparison, so it is a scientifically plausible alternative. It also captures one component of the target mechanism—interface obstruction of dislocations and associated pileups. However, it misses the central nonmonotonic modulation-period experiment, the special role of semicoherent interfaces and misfit dislocations in M16, proposed stress-induced interfacial amorphization, and the resulting low-stress-exponent diffusion/interface-slip regime. Its generic untreated baseline cannot reveal the coherent–semicoherent–grain-boundary distinction. The operating conditions conflict directly with the room-temperature 5 mN nanoindentation boundary. The cited evidence concerns γ/γ′ high-entropy superalloys or bulk elevated-temperature HEA creep and therefore supports only broad claims about interfaces and dislocations, not the specific coating mechanism.
